questions.question:
The expenses of the Union Public Service commission including any salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the members or employees of the Commission shall be charged on which of the following?

I Consolidated Fund of India

II. Contingency Funds of India
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only I​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Consolidated Fund of India** is one of the most significant accounts of the Government of India.
 
• It comprises all **revenues (tax and non-tax)** received by the Government of India, all loans raised, and all money received by repayment of loans.
 
• Expenses related to the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**, including salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to members and employees, are charged on this fund.
 
• Being a charged expenditure, these expenses are not subject to the **vote of Parliament**. This ensures the **independence and autonomy** of UPSC.
 
• The provision for charging these expenses is made under **Article 322** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This constitutional safeguard reinforces the importance of UPSC in maintaining a fair and transparent recruitment process for civil services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Contingency Fund of India**__

 
 
• The **Contingency Fund of India** is used for meeting urgent, unforeseen expenditures that cannot wait for approval by Parliament.
 
• It is placed at the disposal of the **President of India**, who can authorize the expenditure from the fund to address emergencies.
 
• The amount spent from this fund must later be authorized by Parliament and replenished.
 
• Unlike the **Consolidated Fund of India**, this fund is not used for regular expenses like those of UPSC.

questions.question: India's highest literary award, given annually to authors for the best creative literary writing in any of the 22 "scheduled languages" recognised in the Indian Constitution and, since 2013, in the English language.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gyanpith Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gyanpith Award is India's highest literary honor, awarded annually to authors for their exceptional creative literary work in any of the 22 "scheduled languages" recognized in the Indian Constitution.
 
• Established in **1961** by the Bharatiya Jnanpith organization, the award aims to celebrate literary excellence and contributions to Indian literature.
 
• Since **2013**, the scope of the award has also been extended to works written in the English language, broadening its inclusivity.
 
• The award includes a cash prize, a citation plaque, and a bronze replica of Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of knowledge and arts.
 
• Renowned authors such as **Shivaram Karanth, Mahasweta Devi, and Girish Karnad** have been recipients of this prestigious honor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award:**

 
 
• A distinguished literary award established in **1954** by the Sahitya Akademi to recognize outstanding books in 24 Indian languages.
 
• This award is different from the Gyanpith Award and does not include works written in English.
 
 
 
• **Saraswati Samman:**
 
 
• Instituted in **1991** by the K.K. Birla Foundation, the Saraswati Samman honors literary works in any Indian language.
 
• It is awarded for a work published within the last 10 years and is considered one of the most prestigious literary awards in India.
 
 
 
• **Youth Award:**
 
 
• This is not a recognized or notable literary award in India; the term is often associated with sports or social achievements.
 
 
 
• **Languages in the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution recognizes **22 scheduled languages** under the Eighth Schedule, which include Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Urdu, and others.
 
• These languages play a crucial role in India's cultural and literary heritage.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same land field in a definite pattern?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inter-cropping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inter-cropping** is the agricultural practice of growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same piece of land in a defined spatial arrangement.
 
• This technique ensures the efficient utilization of resources such as light, water, and nutrients, improving productivity and sustainability.
 
• Crops are planted in a systematic pattern, such as alternate rows or blocks, to avoid competition and maximize benefits.
 
• Common examples of inter-cropping include growing legumes with cereals (e.g., maize and beans) or combining shallow-rooted crops with deep-rooted crops.
 
• It helps reduce the risk of complete crop failure due to pests or diseases, as multiple crops are grown together, offering diversity.
 
• Farmers adopt this method to enhance soil fertility, particularly by incorporating nitrogen-fixing crops like legumes into the cropping system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aeroponics:**

 
 
• A method of growing plants without soil, where plant roots are suspended in the air and sprayed with a nutrient-rich solution.
 
• It is used primarily in controlled environments like greenhouses for crops such as lettuce, herbs, and strawberries.
 
• Aeroponics minimizes water use and enhances nutrient absorption but is not related to inter-cropping.
 
 
 
• **Hydroponics:**
 
 
• A soil-less cultivation technique where plants grow in water containing dissolved nutrients.
 
• Hydroponics is ideal for urban farming and indoor agriculture but does not involve planting multiple crops together in a systematic pattern.
 
• Examples include growing spinach, tomatoes, and cucumbers in hydroponic systems.
 
 
 
• **Monocropping:**
 
 
• Refers to cultivating a single crop on a piece of land year after year, leading to soil degradation and nutrient depletion.
 
• Unlike inter-cropping, monocropping lacks diversity and is more susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• Crops like wheat, rice, and corn are commonly grown using this technique.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Inter-cropping:**
 
 
• Improves **yield stability** by diversifying crop production.
 
• Enhances **soil fertility** through nitrogen fixation by legumes.
 
• Minimizes the **spread of pests and diseases** due to crop diversity.
 
• Promotes **sustainable agriculture** by efficient use of natural resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Inter-cropping is widely practiced in **developing countries** like India due to its economic and ecological benefits.
 
• It is a key component of **integrated farming systems**, which aim to maximize productivity while conserving resources.
 
• Examples of inter-cropping systems include the **three sisters method** (corn, beans, and squash) in Native American farming practices.
 
• Scientific studies have shown that inter-cropping can **increase productivity by up to 20-30%** compared to monocropping.
 
• Government programs like **National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture** promote inter-cropping as a climate-resilient farming practice.

questions.question: What is the molecular mass of an ozone molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**48**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular formula of ozone is **O₃**, which means it consists of three oxygen atoms.
 
• The atomic mass of one oxygen atom (O) is approximately **16 atomic mass units (amu)**.
 
• To find the molecular mass of ozone (O₃), we need to sum the atomic masses of all the oxygen atoms present in the molecule: **3 * 16 amu = 48 amu**.
 
• Hence, the molecular mass of an ozone molecule is **48 amu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Mass:**

 
 
• Molecular mass (or molecular weight) is the mass of a given molecule, calculated as the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the molecule.
 
• It is usually expressed in atomic mass units (amu) or Daltons (Da).
 
• For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) is calculated as 2*(1 amu) + 16 amu = 18 amu.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The atomic mass of an element is the mass of a single atom of the element, typically expressed in atomic mass units (amu).
 
• It is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom (the mass number).
 
• For example, the atomic mass of carbon is approximately 12 amu.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃):**
 
 
• Ozone is a molecule composed of three oxygen atoms.
 
• It is a highly reactive and unstable form of oxygen, with a strong oxidizing ability.
 
• Ozone is found naturally in the Earth's stratosphere and forms the ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.question: JJ Thomson is known for developing which model in 1898?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plum Pudding Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• J.J. Thomson proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** of the atom in 1898 after his discovery of the electron in 1897.
 
• According to this model, the atom is composed of a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it, resembling a "plum pudding."
 
• The model suggested that the positive charge is uniformly distributed throughout the atom, balancing the negative charge of the electrons.
 
• It was the first model to include the electron, an important step in understanding atomic structure.
 
• This model was later disproved by Ernest Rutherford’s Gold Foil Experiment in 1909, which led to the discovery of the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron Discovery:**

 
 
• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through his experiments with cathode rays.
 
• This discovery established that atoms are divisible and contain smaller subatomic particles.
 
 
 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:**
 
 
• In 1909, Ernest Rutherford conducted the Gold Foil Experiment, which demonstrated that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
 
• This experiment invalidated the Plum Pudding Model, leading to the Nuclear Model of the atom.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Model Evolution:**
 
 
• The Plum Pudding Model was an early attempt to explain atomic structure but lacked experimental support for the arrangement of charges.
 
• It was followed by Rutherford’s Nuclear Model and later by Niels Bohr’s Planetary Model.
 
 
 
• **Modern Atomic Theory:**
 
 
• The current understanding of atomic structure is based on quantum mechanics, incorporating the wave-particle duality of electrons and probabilistic electron clouds.

questions.question: Who among the following helped Akbar in formulating a vision of governance based on the idea of ​​Sulh-e-Kul?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abul Fazal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Abul Fazal**, one of the nine gems (Navratnas) in Emperor Akbar's court, played a significant role in shaping Akbar's ideas on governance, including the concept of **Sulh-e-Kul** (universal peace).
 
• Sulh-e-Kul emphasized **tolerance, harmony, and inclusivity** across all religions and communities, forming the foundation of Akbar's secular policies.
 
• Abul Fazal was the author of the **Akbarnama** and the **Ain-i-Akbari**, which documented Akbar's reign and policies, including the principles of Sulh-e-Kul.
 
• He acted as Akbar's close advisor, shaping the emperor's vision of governance based on justice and equality, irrespective of religious distinctions.
 
• The Sulh-e-Kul policy aimed to create a peaceful and unified empire by promoting religious tolerance and curbing sectarian conflicts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sulh-e-Kul**:

 
 
• It translates to "universal peace" and was Akbar's principle of governance that encouraged harmony among diverse religious and ethnic groups.
 
• This policy reflected Akbar's vision of a secular and inclusive state, ensuring fair treatment of all citizens regardless of religion.
 
 
 
• **Abul Fazal's Role**:
 
 
• He was a Persian scholar, historian, and statesman in Akbar's court.
 
• His writings, especially the Ain-i-Akbari, provided detailed insights into Akbar's administration and policies.
 
 
 
• **Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari**:
 
 
• The Akbarnama is a historical account of Akbar's reign, while the Ain-i-Akbari is an administrative manual covering Akbar's policies and governance system.
 
• These works highlight Akbar's innovative ideas, including Sulh-e-Kul, as a hallmark of his rule.
 
 
 
• **Navratnas (Nine Gems)**:
 
 
• These were the nine extraordinary talents in Akbar's court, including Abul Fazal, Birbal, Raja Todarmal, Faizi, and others.
 
• They contributed significantly to the cultural, administrative, and intellectual achievements of Akbar's reign.
 
 
 
• **Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi**:
 
 
• Din-i-Ilahi (Religion of God) was a syncretic religious movement initiated by Akbar to merge the best practices of various religions.
 
• It symbolized his commitment to Sulh-e-Kul and religious tolerance.

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the term Culture Fishery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Farming of the fishes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Culture Fishery** refers to the **controlled farming of fish**, where the growth and production of fish are enhanced by human intervention in a controlled environment such as ponds, tanks, or other artificial water bodies.
 
• The primary purpose of culture fishery is to **increase fish production** to meet the demand for seafood and to provide a source of livelihood to individuals engaged in aquaculture.
 
• This type of fishery involves techniques such as **breeding, rearing, and harvesting of fish** in artificial or semi-natural water bodies.
 
• Culture fishery is a part of **aquaculture**, which also includes farming of other aquatic organisms like crustaceans, mollusks, and aquatic plants.
 
• It plays a critical role in **sustainable fish production**, ensuring a consistent supply of fish while reducing pressure on natural water bodies and marine ecosystems.
 
• Examples of fish species commonly used in culture fishery include **Rohu, Catla, Mrigal, Tilapia, and Carp**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Fisheries:**

 
 
• **Capture Fishery:** This involves the harvesting of fish from their natural habitats, such as rivers, lakes, and oceans. It does not involve human intervention in the breeding or rearing of fish.
 
• **Culture Fishery:** This involves the farming of fish in controlled environments like ponds, tanks, or reservoirs, where humans control the conditions for fish growth and reproduction.
 
• **Marine Fishery:** This type of fishery deals with the capture or farming of fish in marine ecosystems, such as oceans and seas.
 
• **Inland Fishery:** This involves the capture and farming of fish in freshwater ecosystems like rivers, lakes, and reservoirs.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Culture Fishery:**
 
 
• It contributes significantly to **food security** by providing a consistent supply of fish protein.
 
• It supports the **economy** by creating livelihood opportunities for farmers and workers in the aquaculture sector.
 
• Culture fishery reduces **overfishing** in natural water bodies, helping to conserve marine biodiversity.
 
• It allows for the production of **high-value fish species** that are in demand in domestic and international markets.
 
 
 
• **Features of Culture Fishery:**
 
 
• It involves the use of **scientific techniques** to monitor water quality, feed quality, and fish health.
 
• Fish farming systems can be classified into **extensive, semi-intensive, and intensive systems** based on the level of human intervention and stocking density.
 
• It often includes practices like **polyculture** (culturing multiple species in the same water body) to optimize resource use and enhance productivity.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Aquaculture:**
 
 
• India is one of the leading producers of fish through aquaculture, ranking **second globally** after China.
 
• Key states involved in culture fisheries include **Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Odisha, and Kerala**.
 
• The government promotes aquaculture through initiatives like the **Blue Revolution Scheme** and the **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Capture and Culture Fisheries:**

 
 
• **Capture Fisheries:** Depend on wild fish populations and are subject to environmental factors and overfishing.
 
• **Culture Fisheries:** Provide controlled conditions for fish farming, ensuring consistent yields and reduced environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges in Culture Fishery:**
 
 
• Maintaining **water quality** and controlling diseases in fish farms.
 
• Ensuring the availability of **quality fish feed** and seeds for farming.
 
• Addressing environmental concerns, such as **water pollution** and the ecological impact of intensive aquaculture practices.

__

• The state is rich in biodiversity and has numerous **unique cultural festivals**.

• These dances are performed in colorful attire and reflect tribal customs and folklore.

questions.question: Which of the following words is not part of Article 15 of the Indian Constitution as far as grounds of discrimination are concerned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Profession**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, and place of birth**.
 
• The term "profession" is not mentioned in Article 15 as a ground for discrimination.
 
• This article ensures that every citizen has equal access to public places and institutions, irrespective of the specified grounds.
 
• The provision also extends to the state, ensuring that no citizen is discriminated against in the matter of public employment or office under the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14:**

 
 
• Ensures equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• It prohibits any discrimination by the state against any person.
 
 
 
• **Article 16:**
 
 
• Provides for equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• No citizen can be discriminated against in respect of employment or office under the state on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them.
 
 
 
• **Article 17:**
 
 
• Abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• It is a direct outcome of the principle of equality enshrined in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 18:**
 
 
• Abolishes titles and makes it a punishable offense to confer or accept any title, except military or academic distinctions.
 
• Ensures that the principle of equality is maintained and that there is no aristocracy or elitism in the society.

questions.question: What do ‘check dams’ refer to?

options.text: Earthen or concrete structures across flooded gullies
Dams built only for industrial water supply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthen or concrete structures across flooded gullies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Check dams** are small, usually temporary or permanent barriers constructed across a **swale**, **drainage ditch**, or **gully**. They are primarily designed to counteract **erosion** by reducing the **velocity of water flow** during heavy rains or floods.
 
• These structures can be built using various materials, most commonly **earthen embankments**, **reinforced concrete**, **loose stones** (gabions), or **timber**. The choice of material depends on the **topography** and the intensity of water flow in the region. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The main functional objective of a check dam is to **trap sediment** and allow **surface runoff** to seep into the ground, thereby facilitating **groundwater recharge**. This makes them a vital component of **watershed management**.
 
• By slowing down the water, check dams prevent the deepening of **gullies** and the loss of fertile **topsoil**, which is crucial for **agricultural productivity** in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
• Unlike large-scale dams, check dams are **cost-effective**, have a **low environmental impact**, and can often be constructed using **local community labor** and resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rainwater Harvesting:**

 
 
• Check dams are a form of **in-situ rainwater harvesting**. They help in increasing the **water table** levels in nearby wells, providing a reliable source of water for **irrigation** during dry months.
 
• In **India**, states like **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, and **Maharashtra** extensively use check dams to combat **drought** conditions and manage **water scarcity**.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Impact:**
 
 
• By creating small pools of standing water, these structures support **local biodiversity**, providing **hydration** for livestock and wildlife.
 
• They also help in **pollutant filtration**, as the slower water movement allows **heavy metals** and **nutrients** to settle with the sediment rather than flowing into larger **river systems**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Small huts near rivers** usually refer to temporary dwellings or **fishing shelters** and have no relation to water engineering.
 
• **Industrial water supply dams** are typically much larger, **permanent reservoirs** designed for high-volume storage rather than erosion control in gullies.
 
• **Crescent-shaped hills** for farming are often related to **contour bunding** or **terrace farming**, which are soil conservation methods but are not "dams" themselves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Maintenance:** One of the critical aspects of check dams is **desiltation**. Over time, the area behind the dam fills with **silt** and **debris**, reducing its capacity to slow water. Periodic removal of this silt (which is often rich in **nutrients**) can be used to improve **farm soil**.
 
• **Design Criteria:** A well-designed check dam must have a **spillway** or a lower center section to allow excess water to pass over without eroding the **flanks** of the structure.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** In **India**, schemes like the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)** and **MGNREGA** provide **funding** and **employment** for the construction of check dams to ensure **sustainable water management**.
 
• **Geographical Location:** They are most effective in **hilly terrains** or regions with **undulating slopes** where **surface runoff** is high and **soil erosion** is a significant threat.

questions.question: Partition of Bengal was announced in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__July 19, 1905__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Partition of Bengal was announced on **19th July 1905**__**.**
 
• **__Reasons for Partition of Bengal__:**
 
 
• The province was too big to be administered, but the real motive was to weaken the **Hindu - Muslim unity**.
 
 
 
• It was partitioned by **Lord Curzon** who was Viceroy of India for the convenience of administration.
 
• Lord Curzon divided Bengal into **Western Bengal and Eastern Bengal **on **October 16, 1905.**
